title: Customers without orders
prompt: Show the name of customers who have never placed an order. Replace the ___.
starterSql:
SELECT c.name
FROM customers c
LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id
WHERE ___;
hints: Keep rows where the right table's key is NULL.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM order_items; DELETE FROM orders; DELETE FROM products; DELETE FROM customers; INSERT INTO customers VALUES (7, 'Ravi', 'Oslo', 'ravi@mail.test', '2024-05-05'), (8, 'Sara', 'Lima', NULL, '2024-06-06'), (9, 'Tom', 'Oslo', NULL, '2024-07-07'); INSERT INTO products VALUES (7, 'Stool', 'Home', 40.0, 25.0), (8, 'Cup', 'Kitchen', 9.0, 2.0), (9, 'Ink', 'Stationery', 12.5, 6.0); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (11, 7, '2024-02-28', 'shipped'), (12, 8, '2024-03-01', 'pending'), (13, 7, '2024-03-31', 'cancelled'); INSERT INTO order_items VALUES (11, 7, 1, 4.0), (11, 8, 3, NULL), (12, 9, 2, NULL), (13, 8, 1, NULL);

solutions: SELECT c.name FROM customers c LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id WHERE o.id IS NULL;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT c.name FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id;
SELECT c.name FROM customers c LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id WHERE o.id = NULL;

title: Empty departments
prompt: Show the name of departments with no employees.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM employees; DELETE FROM departments; INSERT INTO departments VALUES (5, 'Design'), (6, 'Finance'), (7, 'Ops'); INSERT INTO employees VALUES (11, 'Ivy', 5, NULL, 90000, '2019-02-01', 900, 'ivy@acme.test'), (12, 'Jon', 5, 11, 70000, '2020-06-15', NULL, NULL), (13, 'Kim', 6, 11, 70000, '2023-03-03', 300, 'kim@acme.test'), (14, 'Leo', NULL, 77, 30000, '2024-08-20', NULL, 'leo@acme.test'), (15, 'Mia', 6, 13, 55000, '2022-12-31', 0, 'mia@acme.test');

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT d.name FROM departments d JOIN employees e ON e.department_id = d.id;
SELECT e.name FROM employees e WHERE e.department_id IS NULL;

title: Never sold

title: Unused courses
prompt: Show the title of courses with no enrolments.
hints: Check the enrolment id for NULL.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM enrolments; DELETE FROM courses; DELETE FROM students; INSERT INTO students VALUES (6, 'Femi', 9), (7, 'Gia', 9), (8, 'Hao', 10); INSERT INTO courses VALUES (5, 'Chemistry', 'Science'), (6, 'Drama', 'Arts'); INSERT INTO enrolments VALUES (11, 6, 5, 60, '2023-autumn'), (12, 6, 5, 60, '2024-spring'), (13, 7, 5, NULL, '2024-spring'), (14, 7, 6, 95, '2024-spring'); INSERT INTO courses VALUES (9, 'Latin', 'Arts');

solutions: SELECT c.title FROM courses c LEFT JOIN enrolments e ON e.course_id = c.id WHERE e.id IS NULL;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT c.title FROM courses c JOIN enrolments e ON e.course_id = c.id;
SELECT c.title FROM courses c LEFT JOIN enrolments e ON e.course_id = c.id WHERE e.grade IS NULL;

prompt: This should find customers with no orders, but returns nothing because it tests the wrong column. Fix it.
starterSql:
SELECT c.name
FROM customers c
LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id
WHERE c.id IS NULL;
hints: Test a column from the right table.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM order_items; DELETE FROM orders; DELETE FROM products; DELETE FROM customers; INSERT INTO customers VALUES (7, 'Ravi', 'Oslo', 'ravi@mail.test', '2024-05-05'), (8, 'Sara', 'Lima', NULL, '2024-06-06'), (9, 'Tom', 'Oslo', NULL, '2024-07-07'); INSERT INTO products VALUES (7, 'Stool', 'Home', 40.0, 25.0), (8, 'Cup', 'Kitchen', 9.0, 2.0), (9, 'Ink', 'Stationery', 12.5, 6.0); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (11, 7, '2024-02-28', 'shipped'), (12, 8, '2024-03-01', 'pending'), (13, 7, '2024-03-31', 'cancelled'); INSERT INTO order_items VALUES (11, 7, 1, 4.0), (11, 8, 3, NULL), (12, 9, 2, NULL), (13, 8, 1, NULL);

solutions: SELECT c.name FROM customers c LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id WHERE o.id IS NULL;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT c.name FROM customers c LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id;

title: No shipped orders
prompt: Show the name of customers with no shipped order. Customers with only other statuses count as having none.
hints: Filter in ON, then test for NULL.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM order_items; DELETE FROM orders; DELETE FROM products; DELETE FROM customers; INSERT INTO customers VALUES (7, 'Ravi', 'Oslo', 'ravi@mail.test', '2024-05-05'), (8, 'Sara', 'Lima', NULL, '2024-06-06'), (9, 'Tom', 'Oslo', NULL, '2024-07-07'); INSERT INTO products VALUES (7, 'Stool', 'Home', 40.0, 25.0), (8, 'Cup', 'Kitchen', 9.0, 2.0), (9, 'Ink', 'Stationery', 12.5, 6.0); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (11, 7, '2024-02-28', 'shipped'), (12, 8, '2024-03-01', 'pending'), (13, 7, '2024-03-31', 'cancelled'); INSERT INTO order_items VALUES (11, 7, 1, 4.0), (11, 8, 3, NULL), (12, 9, 2, NULL), (13, 8, 1, NULL);

solutions: SELECT c.name FROM customers c LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id AND o.status = 'shipped' WHERE o.id IS NULL;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT c.name FROM customers c LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id WHERE o.id IS NULL;
wrongSolutions.why: Misses customers with only other statuses

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT c.name FROM customers c LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id WHERE o.status <> 'shipped';
wrongSolutions.why: Keeps customers with shipped orders too

title: Visits without purchases
prompt: Show each customer city and how many of its customers never ordered, as inactive. Only list cities with at least one.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM order_items; DELETE FROM orders; DELETE FROM products; DELETE FROM customers; INSERT INTO customers VALUES (7, 'Ravi', 'Oslo', 'ravi@mail.test', '2024-05-05'), (8, 'Sara', 'Lima', NULL, '2024-06-06'), (9, 'Tom', 'Oslo', NULL, '2024-07-07'); INSERT INTO products VALUES (7, 'Stool', 'Home', 40.0, 25.0), (8, 'Cup', 'Kitchen', 9.0, 2.0), (9, 'Ink', 'Stationery', 12.5, 6.0); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (11, 7, '2024-02-28', 'shipped'), (12, 8, '2024-03-01', 'pending'), (13, 7, '2024-03-31', 'cancelled'); INSERT INTO order_items VALUES (11, 7, 1, 4.0), (11, 8, 3, NULL), (12, 9, 2, NULL), (13, 8, 1, NULL);

solutions: SELECT c.city, COUNT(*) AS inactive FROM customers c LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id WHERE o.id IS NULL GROUP BY c.city;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT c.city, COUNT(*) AS inactive FROM customers c GROUP BY c.city;
SELECT c.city, COUNT(o.id) AS inactive FROM customers c LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id WHERE o.id IS NULL GROUP BY c.city;
